walkthroughs.body_html:
Non-examination Assessment: Spoken Language Endorsement — a core area of GCSE English Language.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Non-examination Assessment: Spoken Language Endorsement brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Non-examination Assessment: Spoken Language Endorsement.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between voiced and voiceless sounds?
options: Voiced sounds are loud and voiceless sounds are whispered.
Voiced sounds are produced with vocal-fold vibration (/b/, /d/, /g/, /z/); voiceless sounds without it (/p/, /t/, /k/, /s/). You can feel the difference by putting a hand on your throat.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Voiced sounds use the lips; voiceless sounds use the tongue.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between semantics and pragmatics?
options: Semantics studies literal meaning of words and sentences; pragmatics studies how meaning depends on context, speaker intention and conversational implicature.
Semantics is grammar and pragmatics is vocabulary.
Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Semantics is speech and pragmatics is writing.

mcqs.q: How does Piaget's theory relate language to cognitive development?
options: Piaget was a behaviourist who emphasised reinforcement.
Piaget said language drives cognitive development.

Language develops as a consequence of cognitive development — children must first develop concepts (object permanence, conservation) before they can express them linguistically. Cognition leads language.
Voiced sounds use the lips; voiceless sounds use the tongue.
